gap: No result ChatGPT got gives a current price for any 12 V-adapter alternative to the QNAP TS-233; UGREEN's US store sells the NASync DH2300 for $239.99 today, about the same as the $239 TS-233 card, while TerraMaster's cheapest current 2-bay (F2-425) is $269.99 and the 8× M.2 F8 SSD Plus is $809.99.
standout_why: I compared against the cited QNAP TS-233 hardware-spec page and the Synology DS124/DS223j and DS223/DS223j compare pages. None of them gives a price. ChatGPT's own answer showed two card prices ($239 for the TS-233 and $209.99 for the DS223j) but named no retailer and priced no UGREEN, TerraMaster or Zima option. So our prices only partly add to what the rivals already have. None of the rival pages gives an output voltage for any Synology adapter: Synology lists only 36 W or 60 W and 100–240 V AC.
decides: This confirms the pick rather than changing it. Among products with a published 12 V DC adapter, the QNAP TS-233 (QNAP says 'Minimum 48W adapter (12VDC)', 10.81 W typical) and the UGREEN DH2300 ($239.99 at UGREEN US) cost about the same. The choice between them comes down to measured draw and the software, not price. Why the others lose: the Synology DS124 is a single bay with no redundancy, and Synology states no adapter voltage. The DS223j (16.31 W) and DS223 (17.343 W) draw 51–60% more than the TS-233 under access. The UGREEN DXP2800 costs $150 more than the DH2300 ($389.99). The TerraMaster F8 SSD Plus costs $809.99, more than three times the 2-bay 12 V options.
